patterns: unsaon nga mo gamit ang unsa man
what does man mean in bisaya
entries.answer: Unsa man is a very common Cebuano question, and the man at the end is the part that is easy to miss, because it is not a separate word but a softening particle. Unsa alone asks what in a blunt way, and unsa man asks the same question in an ordinary conversational tone, and the two differ only in that one syllable. It is used both for a real question, as in unsa man ka, and as a general opener, where it means something like so or well, and a learner who translates it literally as what indeed will sometimes be right and sometimes not. The same particle works with other question words, so asa man asks where in a friendly way and kinsa man asks who, and a speaker who leaves it off by accident sounds impatient rather than wrong. It is one of the most useful things a learner can pick up, because it is used constantly in ordinary speech and it is never wrong to include it.
